crop.notes: The top headline is cut: the page shows 'THE PRIZE FIGHT!' above 'Allen Whips McCoole', and the clipping shows only the bottom half of 'Allen Whips McCoole'. The clipping also covers only the first two columns (the trip, the boarding, the island and the ring); the page shows the article continuing into the next column with the fight itself and the foul, which is not in the clipping.

ocr.notes: Long text, mostly right with many small letter errors; the first headline line is missing from the transcript and the subheads are partly garbled.

title.suggested: Allen Whips McCoole, but McCoole Wins on a Foul

summary.suggested: The Daily Missouri Democrat described the trip to Tom Allen's fight with Mike McCoole on Foster's Island, 26 miles from St. Louis, headlining that Allen whipped McCoole but the referee declared a foul and McCoole won the money.

metadata.notes: The masthead reads 'Daily Democrat. Wednesday Morning, June 16, 1869.' This is before the 1875 merger, so it is not the Globe-Democrat.

facts.fact: Allen fought Mike McCoole on Foster's Island in the Mississippi, 26 miles below St. Louis; the paper headlined that Allen whipped McCoole but the referee declared a foul and McCoole won the money
places: Foster's Island, Mississippi River, 26 miles from St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen boarded the fight steamer Louisville off the Kingsland iron works with his trainer Sherman Thurston, in the skiff Lady Franklin
Before the fight Allen said he weighed only 170 pounds against McCoole's 218, and that he had come to McCoole's own city to fight him
facts.quote: If I can stay till those get big I'll win. I want to whip him if I am the best man; I have given him every chance; I came here to his own place to fight him, and I ask no favors. But he can't win anyway. Yes, he is bigger; I weigh only 170; but then you will see.

notes: needs_human because the clipping stops before the fight account: the rounds, the foul and the 'pistols and knives' in the headlines are in the next column and should be re-cropped. The facts on the result come only from the headlines. The excursion took in $2,533, leaving $2,238 for the winner; McCoole's barkeeper Tom Kehoe and Billy Carroll took tickets. Allen hardened his hands by soaking them in copperas and horseradish.
